title: SAVOR: Self-Aware Visual Grounding via Confidence-Calibrated Reinforcement Learning for Multimodal Hallucination Mitigation
method: Confidence-augmented outputs and a GRPO objective that penalises calibration error and poor abstention; confidence used at inference to revisit evidence.
dataset: 50K LLaVA-Instruct samples reformatted; pseudo-labelled confidences; InternVL3-8B, Qwen3-VL-8B.
findings: Lower hallucination and lower ECE than DPO and decoding baselines.
limits: No limitations section found.

title: DEEPO: Dual-Entropy Enhanced Policy Optimization for Hallucination in MLLMs
method: Semantic-entropy-triggered expert prefixes plus advantage-sign-aware Renyi preconditioning.
dataset: Prefixes from dataset traces or verified rollouts; four training seeds.
findings: Both branches beat GRPO; interaction significant on VideoMMMU (+4.0).
limits: No limitations section found.

title: Staying VIGILant: Mitigating Visual Laziness via Counterfactual Visual Alignment in MLLMs
method: VIGIL: RL post-training that maximises visual-response mutual information and penalises blind confidence under attention masking.
dataset: Preference data (uses 25% of the data of state-of-the-art methods).
findings: Beats recent alignment methods with 25% of the data; models 7B-72B.
limits: Authors: counterfactual built by zero-out masking only.

title: VL-Calibration: Decoupled Confidence Calibration for Large Vision-Language Models Reasoning
method: Decoupled confidence calibration trained with RL (VL-Calibration).
dataset: 13 benchmarks.
findings: ECE 0.421 to 0.098; accuracy +2.3 to +3.0%.
limits: No limitations section found.

title: Teaching MLLMs to Say No: Generalized Referring Expression Comprehension via Refusal Calibrated GRPO
method: Refusal-calibrated GRPO for generalized referring expression comprehension.
dataset: gRefCOCO and related no-target sets.
findings: Precision 45.0 to 62.2 (AP 26.4 to 34.0) in one setting; 53.5 to 60.5 on gRefCOCO.
limits: No limitations section found.

title: MMBoundary: Advancing MLLM Knowledge Boundary Awareness through Reasoning Step Confidence Calibration
method: Self-rewarding step-level confidence signals (textual and cross-modal), SFT warm-up for confidence expression, then RL with several reward functions for calibration.
dataset: Reasoning-chain annotated data (section 4.2).
findings: Better step-level confidence calibration and fewer snowballed errors (authors).
limits: Limitation section: relies on internal states and uncertainty estimates to assess confidence.

title: Improving Vision-language Models with Perception-centric Process Reward Models
method: Perceval: a trained process reward model that extracts image-related claims, checks each against the image and returns hallucinated spans; token-level advantages in GRPO; also used
dataset: Perception-intensive supervised data to train Perceval (sizes not extracted).
findings: Gains on several benchmarks across reasoning VLMs; better than majority voting for test-time scaling.
limits: Authors: not stated as a section; it needs a separately trained reward model (reviewer note).

title: CORA: Analyzing and bridging thinking-answer gap in Multimodal RLVR via Consistency-Oriented Reasoning Alignment
method: Lightweight plug-and-play consistency reward model + Hybrid Reward Advantage Splitting (HRAS) in GRPO.
dataset: Training sets: PuzzleVQA-style set (6.5K), Math-40K, CV-Bench training data; several Qwen LVLMs.
findings: Improves task performance and reduces thinking-answer inconsistency; more faithful traces.
limits: Authors: only models up to 7B tested; image-text only, no video.

title: CFPO: Counterfactual Policy Optimization for Multimodal Reasoning
method: Cross-modal counterfactual regulariser: maximise the gap between predictions and a state with critical visual cues suppressed; plugs into GRPO/DAPO; no external reward model.
dataset: Standard multimodal RL training data (e.g. Geo3K-style sets); sizes not extracted.
findings: +3.17 to +6.25% over standard RL baselines; +1.32 to +2.13% over PAPO.
limits: Authors: extra computational cost (Appendix B).

title: V-Rubrics: Visual Faithfulness via Rubric-Based Reinforcement Learning
method: Atomic-proposition rubrics scoring Visual Faithfulness, Reasoning Consistency and Instruction Following; prefix-localised credit in GRPO.
dataset: V-Rubrics 50K built from 17 sources and annotated with Gemini-3-Pro; SFT on OpenMMReasoner-SFT-874K; Qwen3-VL-8B.
findings: Beats SFT and answer-only GRPO; largest gains on knowledge-oriented and visually grounded benchmarks.
limits: Authors: rubric quality and judge verification; approximate prefix-credit localisation.

title: DRT: Dense Reasoning Trace for Efficient and Grounded Multimodal Reasoning
method: Dense structured traces and Trace-Grounded GRPO with structured rewards.
dataset: Reference traces from a tri-perspective verification pipeline; Qwen3-VL-8B.
findings: 5.5x token efficiency and +1.3 accuracy points over Qwen3-VL.
limits: No limitations section found (checklist text only).

title: MIRL: Mutual Information-Guided Reinforcement Learning for Vision-Language Models
method: Mutual-information-based selection of pre-sampled descriptions, forking, and decoupled perception/reasoning rewards.
dataset: Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct; training set with complete trajectories and descriptions.
findings: Fewer full trajectories needed for gains; decoupled reward resolves reward blindness (as framed by the authors).
limits: Appendix validates MI as a quality indicator across models; no limitations section found.

title: Visually-Guided Policy Optimization for Multimodal Reasoning
method: VGPO: visual attention compensation and visual-focus reinforcement inside RLVR.
dataset: Qwen2.5-VL 3B/7B/32B; trained on Geo3K and other sizes.
findings: Beats DAPO even in data-constrained settings.
limits: No limitations section found.

title: V-tableR1: Process-Supervised Multimodal Table Reasoning with Critic-Guided Policy Optimization
method: Process-supervised RL with a critic that scores reasoning steps (V-tableR1).
dataset: Seven tabular datasets including TabFact and InfoTabs; Qwen 4B model.
findings: Up to +10.6% over SFT.
limits: No limitations section found.

title: AnE: Pushing the Reasoning Frontier of Multimodal LLMs via Anchor Evolution
method: Anchor-and-explore RL (AnE) with truth-grounded anchors.
dataset: Eight benchmarks incl. MathVista, MathVision, MathVerse, LogicVista, ScienceQA, MMMU, EMMA.
findings: +10.3% across eight benchmarks.
limits: No limitations section found.

title: Perceptual Flow Network for Visually Grounded Reasoning
method: Perceptual Flow Network: variational RL with multi-dimensional perception rewards, Qwen3-VL-8B base.
dataset: V*, TreeBench, MME-RealWorld-lite.
findings: Gains of 13.1%, 10.4% and 21% on the three benchmarks.
limits: No limitations section found.

title: Improving Visual Reasoning with Iterative Evidence Refinement
method: Iterative evidence refinement trained with GRPO (SIEVE) on Qwen3-VL-4B/8B.
dataset: MME-Real-Lite, RealWorldQA, MathVista, LogicVista, WeMath, a hallucination benchmark.
findings: Improves visual reasoning and hallucination scores over the base models.
limits: No limitations section found.

title: CPPO: Contrastive Perception Policy Optimization for VLM Agents
method: Contrastive Perception Policy Optimization (CPPO).
dataset: Agent and perception benchmarks (names not extracted).
findings: Average gains of +11.2% and +5.9%.
limits: Limitations appendix present.

title: Think with Structured Grounding: Perceptual Reinforcement Learning for Chart and Visual-Tabular Understanding
method: Think with Structured Grounding: perceptual RL without external tools (TwSG).
dataset: Chart and table benchmarks.
findings: 73.70% average accuracy.
limits: States a limitation: only models of 8B or smaller tested.

title: Consistency as Inductive Bias: Learning Cross-View Invariance for Robust Multimodal Reasoning
method: ConsistRoll: cross-view consistency inside GRPO and Hint-GRPO, Qwen2.5-VL-7B and 3B.
dataset: Math-and-logic, general understanding and hallucination-sensitive evaluations (names not extracted).
findings: Improves both GRPO and Hint-GRPO on both model sizes.
limits: Limitations appendix (E) present.

title: Reinforcing Multimodal Reasoning Against Visual Degradation
method: RL that learns from successful trajectories under corrupted images, Qwen3-VL 4B/8B.
dataset: About 30K training samples; seven benchmarks (MathVista, WeMath, ChartQA, LogicVista, MMStar, VisualPuzzles, RealWorldQA).
findings: Robustness +2.4% (seen) and +2.3% (unseen) over GRPO, clean accuracy matched.
limits: No limitations section found.

title: Be Faithful When Response: Returning Fluent and Grounded Answers for Vision-Language Models Reinforcement Learning
method: Faithful Warm-Start (FWS): build FaithfulQA by curating samples with explicit vision-language causal links from six general VQA sets, filter with a VLM judge, warm-start the policy
dataset: FaithfulQA (derived from six general VQA benchmarks, e.g. ChartQA, AI2D, ScienceQA); Qwen3-VL backbone.
findings: Warm-starting toward faithful reasoning before RL stabilises training and improves grounded answers (authors).
limits: Only a Future Work section; no limitations section. Depends on a VLM judge to purify the data.

title: Understanding the Role of Hallucination in Reinforcement Post-Training of Multimodal Reasoning Models
method: Hallucination-as-Cue analysis: modality-specific corruptions that remove information needed for the answer, used in training and inference (GRPO).
dataset: Standard RL post-training data with corruptions; Qwen2.5-VL 3B/7B.
findings: Training on corrupted (hallucination-inducing) data can still improve reasoning, which questions how much RL uses the image (authors).
limits: No limitations section found.

title: CAVE: A Structured Credit Assignment Approach for Fragmented Visual Evidence Reasoning
method: Structured process reward on GRPO scoring belief update, evidence acquisition and adaptive focus control at the action level; TRACER-Bench.
dataset: TRACER-Bench (authors) and public benchmarks.
findings: Improves fragmented visual evidence tasks on public and new benchmarks (authors).
limits: Appendix G: only open-source models at moderate scale.

title: More Than the Final Answer: Improving Visual Extraction and Logical Consistency in Vision-Language Models
method: PeRL-VL: VLM-based description reward scoring self-generated descriptions for faithfulness and sufficiency; text-only Reasoning SFT stage.
dataset: Logic-rich CoT data (e.g. OpenThought) for SFT; Qwen2.5-VL-7B base.
findings: Average Pass@1 63.3% to 68.8%; beats standard RLVR.
limits: Not stated as a section; uses an extra multimodal judge model (reviewer note).

title: Perception-Aware Policy Optimization for Multimodal Reasoning
method: PAPO: Implicit Perception Loss (KL term) plus Double Entropy Loss, plugged into GRPO/DAPO; no extra data, reward model or teacher.
dataset: Same training data and rewards as GRPO/DAPO baselines (names not extracted).
findings: +4.4 to +17.5% overall; 30.5% fewer perception errors.
limits: Authors: no scaling beyond 7B or other model families; training efficiency not optimised.

title: Vision-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in Multimodal Large Language Models
method: Cold-start on a 200K multimodal CoT set, then GRPO with a hard-format result reward and Progressive Thinking Suppression Training.
dataset: Vision-R1-cold (200K CoT); 10K multimodal math RL set.
findings: ~6% average gain; Vision-R1-7B 73.5% on MathVista.
limits: No limitations section found.

title: SoTA with Less: MCTS-Guided Sample Selection for Data-Efficient Visual Reasoning Self-Improvement
method: MCTS-measured difficulty selects 11K hard samples for RFT (no distillation).
dataset: 70K open-source examples filtered to 11K (7B) and 7.5K (72B).
findings: +7% average over Qwen2.5-VL-7B; beats larger models.
limits: No limitations section found.

title: VisualPRM: An Effective Process Reward Model for Multimodal Reasoning
method: 8B process reward model scoring steps, used for best-of-N selection; VisualPRM400K data and VisualProcessBench.
dataset: VisualPRM400K (automated); VisualProcessBench (2,866 samples, 26,950 step labels).
findings: +5.9 points on InternVL2.5-78B; beats outcome RMs and self-consistency.
limits: Authors: open MLLMs rarely mark steps wrong (F1 19.2 on negative steps for InternVL2.5-8B).

title: A Survey of Multimodal Hallucination Evaluation and Detection
method: Survey with a faithfulness/factuality taxonomy of hallucination, benchmarks and detection methods.
dataset: Not applicable.
findings: Highlights limitations of current benchmarks and detection methods.
limits: Survey scope is evaluation and detection, not training rewards.

title: ARM-Thinker: Reinforcing Multimodal Generative Reward Models with Agentic Tool Use and Visual Reasoning
method: RL-trained agentic reward model that calls image tools to verify evidence (ARM-Thinker), Qwen2.5-VL-7B.
dataset: Reward-modelling and tool-use benchmarks.
findings: +16.2% on reward-modelling benchmarks and +9.6% on tool use.
limits: No limitations section found (broader-impact section only).

title: Unveiling Chain of Step Reasoning for Vision-Language Models with Fine-grained Rewards
method: Chain of Step (CoS) structured reasoning; ShareGPT-Step-300K with step labels from Monte Carlo estimation and LLM-as-judge; step-level process reward model; iterative DPO and GRPO
dataset: ShareGPT-Step-300K (built by the authors); public vision-language reasoning benchmarks.
findings: Fine-grained step rewards give consistent gains and enable inference-time scaling (authors).
limits: Appendix G: process labels from Monte Carlo and LLM judge are not guaranteed correct; annotation noise remains.

title: DeepEyes: Incentivizing "Thinking with Images" via Reinforcement Learning
method: End-to-end agentic RL (no cold-start SFT) where the model calls its own grounding as an image-zoom tool; reward design and data selection tailored to tool use.
dataset: Curated training data (appendix B); Qwen2.5-VL-7B.
findings: Gains on perception, grounding, hallucination and maths; tool-use evolves from exploration to efficient use (authors).
limits: Appendix E: shortcuts remain (shallow reasoning, imprecise localisation); only Qwen2.5-VL tested.

title: AutoRubric: Rubric-Based Generative Rewards for Faithful Multimodal Reasoning
method: AutoRubric: self-aggregation of reasoning checkpoints from successful trajectories into problem-specific rubrics; an LLM judge scores rubrics; combined with outcome reward in GRPO.
dataset: Training problems with automatically collected rubrics; Qwen2.5-VL-7B.
findings: State-of-the-art on six benchmarks and better reasoning faithfulness (authors).
limits: Limitations section: the judge adds about 40% training time per step.

title: Qwen Look Again: Guiding Vision-Language Reasoning Models to Re-attention Visual Information
method: Balanced Reflective Policy Optimization (BRPO) to decide when to reflect on the image; visual re-attention by re-supplying tokens during reflection or at test time.
dataset: Cold-start data in appendix B; Qwen2.5-VL 7B/32B.
findings: Fewer hallucinations and better accuracy with vision-text reflection (authors).
limits: Section 6 Limitations: the analysis assumes neglect of visual information is a main cause.

title: Learning When to Look: A Disentangled Curriculum for Strategic Perception in Multimodal Reasoning
method: Disentangled SFT curriculum (text-only reasoning first, then perception-grounded CoT), then RL with a pivotal-perception reward that teaches when to look.
dataset: Curriculum SFT data and RL data; Qwen2.5-VL-type backbone.
findings: Better long-chain visual reasoning and perception benchmarks (authors).
limits: No limitations section found.

title: Hallucination of Multimodal Large Language Models: A Survey
method: Literature survey with taxonomy of causes, evaluation and mitigation.
dataset: Not applicable (228 references, per arXiv comment).
findings: Organises causes, benchmarks and mitigation strategies; lists open questions.
limits: Predates the RL-based fixes in this review.

title: HallusionBench: An Advanced Diagnostic Suite for Entangled Language Hallucination and Visual Illusion in Large Vision-Language Models
method: Human-crafted visual-question pairs with control groups.
dataset: 346 images and 1,129 questions (abstract).
findings: Failure modes: language hallucination and visual illusion.
limits: Limitations and Future Work section present.

title: Attend to Evidence: Evidence-Anchored Spatial Attention Supervision for Multimodal RLVR
method: EASE: evidence-region annotations become a visual-token attention target used as process supervision on high-reward trajectories only.
dataset: Training set with single- and multi-region evidence annotations; Qwen2.5-VL-7B, Qwen3-VL-4B/8B.
findings: +2.5 to +3.1 average points over DAPO on three backbones.
limits: Authors: needs evidence annotations (box construction cost); suited to localisable evidence.

title: Faithful-MR1: Faithful Multimodal Reasoning via Anchoring and Reinforcing Visual Attention
method: Anchoring (attention supervised against image regions) + Reinforcing (counterfactual image intervention rewards trajectories that rely on vision).
dataset: Region annotations from an automated annotator (Gemini-3-Flash); Qwen2.5-VL 3B/7B.
findings: Outperforms recent baselines on both backbones with less training data.
limits: Authors: region annotations and extra masked-image forward pass.

title: On Robustness and Chain-of-Thought Consistency of RL-Finetuned VLMs
method: Controlled perturbation study (misleading captions, wrong CoT) on RL-finetuned and closed models.
dataset: Spatial VQA sets: 3DSRBench, CV-Bench, Spatial-MM, WhatsUp.
findings: Accuracy-faithfulness tradeoff: more RL steps raise headline accuracy while consistency worsens.
limits: Calls for evaluation that goes beyond accuracy.

title: Metric-Driven Reinforcement Learning for Object Hallucination Reduction in LVLM-Based Image Captioning
method: Captioning as an MDP; Object Consistency Score (F1 of object precision and recall) as reward, token-level KL regularisation, lightweight PPO with a shared frozen backbone and soft-
dataset: COCO (CHAIR) and Visual Genome (CCEval); object lists from dataset annotations or YOLO detectors; InstructBLIP (Vicuna-7B) and LLaVA.
findings: Up to 41% fewer hallucinated captions on COCO and 29% on Visual Genome; caption quality kept or improved; generalises to LLaVA.
limits: Authors: reward quality depends on object-detector accuracy; single training run per model; one day on 8 A6000 GPUs.

title: Where Do Long Captions Fail? Position-Aware Diagnosis and Reinforcement Learning for Detailed Image Captioning
method: Position-aware diagnosis and GRPO with a rubric-based reward (PAGER) on Qwen3-VL-4B.
dataset: PixMo-derived captions.
findings: Beats CapRL on long-caption faithfulness; benefit concentrated at later positions.
limits: Has a "Discussion and limitations" section.

title: VCap: Hypergeometric Rewards for Weak-to-Strong Visual Captioning
method: Witness-adjudicator reward with hypergeometric scoring for GRPO captioning (VCap), 8B model.
dataset: AI2D, MMStar, RealWorldQA, V*.
findings: Matches CapRL on average (66.58 vs 66.56), i.e. no clear gain.
limits: No limitations section found.

title: Beyond Saying Less: Fine-Grained Alignment for Informative and Faithful Vision-Language Models
method: On-policy RL with fine-grained rewards against object hallucination.
dataset: AMBER and related benchmarks; Qwen3.6-27B used as judge.
findings: Reduces hallucination without shortening captions.
limits: Limitations appendix present.

title: CGC: Compositional Grounded Contrast for Fine-Grained Multi-Image Understanding
method: Compositional Grounded Contrast (CGC): multi-image instances built from single-image grounding annotations plus a rule-based spatial reward inside GRPO (Think-before-Grounding).
dataset: MIG-Bench and VLM2-Bench; transfer to MathVista, MuirBench, MMStar, MMMU, BLINK; Qwen3-VL-8B base.
findings: State of the art on MIG-Bench and VLM2-Bench; +2.90 MathVista, +2.88 MuirBench, +1.93 MMStar over the base model.
limits: No limitations section found.

title: Difference Feedback: Generating Multimodal Process-Level Supervision for VLM Reinforcement Learning
method: Repair erroneous trajectories to build token/step-level masks (Difference Feedback), injected into GRPO (DF-GRPO) and PPO (DF-PPO) without step annotations.
dataset: Model-repaired trajectories; Qwen2.5-VL-7B/32B/72B and InternVL backbones.
findings: About 3% average improvement under matched compute (authors).
limits: Section 6: misaligned minimal edits and dependence on the repair model producing correct short edits.

title: Ground What You See: Hallucination-Resistant MLLMs via Caption Feedback, Diversity-Aware Sampling, and Conflict Regularization
method: Plan-and-caption stage with a quality-based caption reward; reward-variance-guided sample selection; NTK-based conflict-aware regularisation (GRPO).
dataset: Open multimodal training data; InternVL-family backbones.
findings: Reduces hallucination during RL and improves benchmark accuracy (authors).
limits: No limitations section found.

title: Reinforcing Consistency in Video MLLMs with Structured Rewards
method: Compositional consistency audit, then sequence-level RL with a structured reward built from anchored factual and temporal claims parsed from captions.
dataset: Caption-derived structured units; Qwen2.5-VL-7B and Qwen3-VL.
findings: Structured consistency rewards improve grounding and general video benchmarks (authors).
limits: No limitations section found.

title: Saliency-R1: Enforcing Interpretable and Faithful Vision-language Reasoning via Saliency-map Alignment Reward
method: Token-level saliency maps via logits decomposition; reward = overlap between saliency and human-annotated boxes; GRPO.
dataset: Public VQA training data with box annotations; Qwen2.5-VL 3B/7B.
findings: Improves faithfulness and interpretability and general VQA (authors).
limits: Section 5 Limitation and Conclusion (heading present).

title: Perception-R1: Advancing Multimodal Reasoning Capabilities of MLLMs via Visual Perception Reward
method: Visual perception reward: a judging LLM scores consistency between visual annotations taken from CoT trajectories and the response, added to the accuracy reward.
dataset: 1,442 training samples.
findings: State of the art on most benchmarks with only 1,442 samples.
limits: Not stated as a section; needs a judge LLM (reviewer note).

title: PROPA: Toward Process-level Optimization in Visual Reasoning via Reinforcement Learning
method: MCTS-guided GRPO producing dense step-level rewards without annotation, interleaved with SFT to fix cold start; a PRM for test-time search.
dataset: Seven benchmarks, four VLM backbones; self-generated MCTS data.
findings: Gains across seven benchmarks and four backbones over SFT and GRPO (authors).
limits: No limitations section found.

title: DeFacto: Counterfactual Thinking with Images for Enforcing Evidence-Grounded and Faithful Reasoning
method: Positive, counterfactual and random-masking training; language-guided evidence region construction (DeFacto-100K); GRPO with three rewards for answer, structure and evidence select
dataset: DeFacto-100K (authors); DeFacto-1.5K human-annotated benchmark.
findings: Improves evidence-grounded consistency beyond accuracy (authors).
limits: No limitations section found; an impact statement only.

title: CodeV: Code with Images for Faithful Visual Reasoning via Tool-Aware Policy Optimization
method: Faithfulness protocol that checks whether visual tool outputs contain the queried evidence; Tool-Aware Policy Optimization (TAPO) adds dense rewards on tool inputs and outputs to G
dataset: Visual-search and reasoning data with code-based tools; Qwen2.5-VL-7B/32B.
findings: Higher faithful tool-use rate and accuracy than prior visual agents (authors).
limits: Limitations section: static judge model adds cost; judge design limits.

title: From Illusion to Intention: Visual Rationale Learning for Vision-Language Reasoning
method: Visual Rationale Learning (ViRL): process supervision with ground-truth rationales, step-level reward shaping, and fine-grained credit assignment (PPO/DAPO-style RL).
dataset: Process-grounded dataset built by the authors (appendix B); Qwen2.5-VL-7B.
findings: More effective visual actions and higher perception accuracy (authors).
limits: Appendix F: small dataset focused on perception-driven reasoning.

title: Reasoning-Aligned Perception Decoupling for Scalable Multi-modal Reasoning
method: RAPID decouples perception (MLLM writes detailed captions) from reasoning (external text-only LLM); Visual Perception Optimization (VPO) rewards the MLLM by the correctness of the
dataset: Caption and QA training data; Qwen2.5-VL 3B/7B/32B/72B and others.
findings: Faithful, query-relevant captions that transfer across reasoners and MLLMs (authors).
limits: Appendix A: no auto-thinking switch; architecture is domain-specific in its current design.

title: PaLMR: Towards Faithful Visual Reasoning via Multimodal Process Alignment
method: Perception-aligned data layer (pseudo ground truth + verifiable visual facts) and process-aligned optimisation: hierarchical reward fusion with a process-aware score inside V-GRPO.
dataset: Process-aware reasoning data built by their pipeline; Qwen2.5-VL-7B backbone.
findings: Reduces reasoning hallucinations; state-of-the-art on HallusionBench while keeping MMMU/MathVista/MathVerse.
limits: Authors: bounded by base-model perception; exact-match reward penalises semantically equivalent wording.

title: Addressing Overthinking in Large Vision-Language Models via Gated Perception-Reasoning Optimization
method: Perception-aware RL objective (GPRO).
dataset: Five benchmarks.
findings: MathVista +6.0%; MathVerse +1.8% with responses 51.5% shorter.
limits: No limitations section found.

title: Iterative Visual Thinking and the Self-Correction Mirage in VLM Grounding
method: Analysis of GRPO with an IoU reward and label-free stopping rules, Qwen3-VL-4B.
dataset: About 2,400 training samples; single-object referring expression comprehension.
findings: Iterating collapses accuracy; best policy is not to iterate (step 0 matches the base).
limits: Limitations stated: one model family, small scale, single GPU, single-object task.

title: Reinforcement Learning with Robust Rubric Rewards
method: Reinforcement learning with robust rubric rewards (RLR3), deterministic verification of rubrics generated by frontier models.
dataset: Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B; 15 benchmarks; ViRL, DeepVision, OpenMMR training sets.
findings: +4.7 points over the base model and above RLVR.
limits: Limitations stated: rubrics depend on an external frontier model; smaller margin on OpenMMR (visual puzzles).

title: PerceptRL: Making Visual Perception Rewardable in MLLMs from Answers to Interactions
method: Perception RL: extract verified errors from dense captions and convert them into QA pairs with fixed labels and rule-based rewards (chain and multiple-choice QA); Perception Agenti
dataset: Pipeline-generated perception QA; Qwen3-VL backbone.
findings: Verifiable perception rewards improve perception benchmarks beyond answer-only RL (authors).
limits: No limitations section found; scattered mentions only.

title: SCOUT: Unlocking Enhanced Spatial Reasoning via Structured Chain-of-Thought and Multi-Objective Process Reward
method: Structured CoT that models 3D perception, multi-objective process rewards and segment-wise advantage estimation (GRPO variant); SCOUT-24k dataset.
dataset: SCOUT-24k (authors, synthesised); Qwen2.5-VL 3B and 7B.
findings: Better spatial reasoning with process rewards (authors).
limits: Appendix: only 3B and 7B models; datasets rely on bounding-box style annotations.

title: COPO: Causal-Oriented Policy Optimization for Hallucinations of MLLMs
method: Token-level causal-completeness reward and a causally informed advantage inside GRPO.
dataset: Not clearly extracted.
findings: Reports gains across benchmarks (abstract gives no numbers).
limits: No limitations section found.

title: Visual-RFT: Visual Reinforcement Fine-Tuning
method: Verifiable perception rewards (e.g. IoU for detection) with GRPO for LVLMs.
dataset: Few-shot fine-grained classification, detection, reasoning grounding sets.
findings: +24.3% one-shot classification; +21.9 COCO two-shot.
limits: No limitations section found.

title: ViCrit: A Verifiable Reinforcement Learning Proxy Task for Visual Perception in VLMs
method: Proxy task: inject one subtle synthetic error into a 200-word human caption and train the VLM to localise the corrupted span, with a binary exact-match reward (GRPO). Also releases
dataset: Captions with injected errors; ViCrit-Bench (images across domains, annotated hallucination categories).
findings: Training on the proxy task transfers to perception and reasoning benchmarks and to hallucination metrics (authors).
limits: No limitations section found.

title: Perceptual-Evidence Anchored Reinforced Learning for Multimodal Reasoning
method: PEARL: derive a perception checklist of verifiable sub-questions per item; auxiliary perception rollouts give a perceptual reward and act as a fidelity gate on the reasoning reward
dataset: Automatically derived perception probes; Qwen2.5-VL 3B/7B/32B.
findings: Gains over vanilla RLVR; reasoning success depends on perception probes (authors).
limits: Section 7: extractable probes per source question are limited.
